## Highlights

- Monitoring history now uses indexed typed facts and logical Ping identities,
  retaining exact current behavior while avoiding repeated JSON expansion and
  cached-probe duplication.
- UTC-aligned resource, network, Ping, traffic, system, and automatic tunnel
  observation tiers bound long-term growth without inventing finer historical
  points. Recent operational status, alerts, and supported billing-cycle
  accounting remain exact.
- Operator and public charts disclose per-domain source resolution, preserve
  missing intervals as gaps, and keep standard time-range curves at or above
  their displayed point density.
- PostgreSQL retention stress projects approximately 22.5 GiB clean at three
  years and 23.8 GiB at the ten-year cap for 30 agents reporting six host
  interfaces, four tunnels, and sixteen Ping targets. Backups, retained WAL,
  and unrelated job artifacts remain separate capacity concerns.

## API and retention changes

- Private and public monitoring responses now use `range.source: "retained"`
  instead of `"minute"` for long-term history. They add
  `requested_step_secs`, `effective_resolution_secs`, `effective_points`, and
  `resolutions.{resources,network,ping,traffic}`. `step_secs` is the actual
  tier-aligned chart step.
- `GET /api/v1/system/dashboard` adds `requested_step_secs`,
  `effective_resolution_secs`, and `effective_points`; `bucket_secs` is now
  range-dependent rather than always 60.
- In `GET /api/v1/history/export`, the `traffic_counter_samples` and
  `network_observations` domain values change from arrays to
  `{ "exact": [...], "tiered": [...] }`.
- `GET /api/v1/network/observation-trends` adds `bucket_start`, `bucket_secs`,
  `retained`, `source_bucket_count`, and `effective_resolution_secs`.
- Accepted high-resolution telemetry now defaults to 7 days. Traffic endpoints
  remain exact for 32 days, while authoritative age-tiered history remains
  available through the configured long-term horizon, 3,650 days by default.
